3. The facts of the plaint of the aforesaid suit, in brief, are that the suit land originally belonged to Satish Chandra Das, who granted settlement of the same along with other lands in favour of Azhar Ali Miah and Mozahar Ali Miah; that in order to recover arrear rents for 1360-1362 BS from the said tenants Azhar and Mozahar, Satis Chandra filed Rent Suit No. 60 of 1957 in the court of the then Munsif, Goalando and that suit was compromised between the parties on 26.02.1957; that pursuant to the said compromise decree, Azhar and Mozahar were admitted as tenants and they remained in possession of the suit land as owner thereof; that Azhar Miah died leaving behind his widow Khodeja, 2 sons- Abdul Latif and Golam Sarwar and one daughter Jahanara Begum as his heirs; that the said heirs of Azhar Ali transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by a registered sale deed being No. 4239 dated 15.06.1982 and delivered possession in his favour; that the suit land became non-cultivable as because of siltation by the flood of 1988; that the ancestral paternal residence of the defendant-opposite party No.1 was in Sujanagar, Pabna and as because of destruction of his house in Pabna by the flood in 1988, he started looking for a piece of land for residential purposes; that the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-2 are the distant relatives of the plaintiff and therefore, the plaintiff allowed them to live in the suit land on a temporary basis given the non-cultivable nature of .the suit land; that accordingly, the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-2 erected homestead in the suit land in the first part of 1989 and started living therein and planted various trees; that at that time the said defendants undertook to vacate the suit land soon after they get another piece of suitable land; that in the middle of November, 2000 they, claimed the title to the suit land on the basis of a kabuliyat from the Government and that even being requested to vacate the suit land, the said defendants refused to do so and hence, the suit. 

 4. The opposite party Nos. 1-2 as defendant Nos. 1-2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that there is no cause of action to bring the present suit and the suit is not maintainable; that the suit is barred by limitation, bad for defect of parties and hit by the provisions of the Court Fees Act; that the suit land belongs to the Government as khas land and as landless peasants they took lease by kabuliyat of the same from the Government on 07.12.1999 for a period of 9 years, which will expire on 28.09.2008; that they got the suit land mutated in their name and they have been enjoying and possessing the same by erecting homestead and planting trees and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 statement denying the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit land has been recorded in the name of the Government as khas land and the same has been settled by leased out in favour of the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-2 by a registered kabuliyat and the suit land has been mutated in their name; that the plaintiff has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 19. Taking to paragraph 7 of the plaint of Title Suit No. 55 of 2000 whereto the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 are the plaintiffs, Mr. Bhuiyan submits that their suit is premature in view of the fact that their so-called kabuliyat was not cancelled, rather the same was merely threatened to be cancelled and such threat of cancellation as opposed to any final decision actually cancelling the lease is not a cause of action and therefore, the said suit being based on a mere apprehension, is without any cause of action and liable to be dismissed.  38. Furthermore, the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs stated in paragraph 7 of the plaint of Title Suit No. 55 of 2000 that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Rajbari Sadar, Rajbari (defendant No. 4 to the said suit) by his letter dated 12.03.2000 merely threatened to cancel his kabuliyat, but at no point of time his lease was actually cancelled, and the threat of cancellation as opposed to any actual cancellation cannot be cause of his grievance and therefore, Title Suit No. 55 of 2000 filed by the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 was held to be premature and liable to be dismissed as being not maintainable in law as per the decision given in the case of Kamaluddin (Md.) and another vs Secretary, Ministry of Land, Bangladesh and others 56 DLR (AD) 212 wherein it has been held that:
